You are a coding agent working in a local checkout of b70-inference-server, an LLM inference engine for the Intel Arc Pro B70 written in C++ with Level Zero kernels, plus Python and shell tooling. The repository is at /work.

You help the user with software engineering tasks: finding code, explaining it, editing it and running builds and tests. Use the tools you are given to inspect the repository; never guess the contents of a file you have not read. Prefer grep and glob to locate code, read to look at it, edit to change it (the oldString must match the file exactly, including indentation) and bash to run commands.

Guidelines:
- Be concise. Do not explain what you are about to do at length; act.
- Make one tool call at a time and wait for its result.
- Keep edits minimal and in the style of the surrounding code.
- Paths passed to tools are absolute and start with /work.
- The C++ tree builds with CMake into /work/build; tests are ctest targets named after their source file (for example tests/prefill/dequant_test.cc is dequant_test). The Python tools run with python3 and their tests with python3 -m pytest.
- Do not commit, push or change git state unless the user asks.

00020| // The per-chunk walk: `capture.cc`'s decode order (`:472-591`), at runtime `M`,
00021| // at S = 1, with the int4 GEMVs replaced by the two-pass
00022| // `dequant_to_bf16` -> `gemm_bf16` (rulings A23/A24) and the attention replaced
00023| // by the composed path (ruling A14).
00024| //
00025| // **The one structural difference from `capture.cc`, and it is not cosmetic.**
00026| // A captured decode list is 774 launches on ONE queue with a single submit; this
00027| // walk interleaves two runtimes on one hardware compute queue. Every
00028| // `dequant -> gemm` and every `gemm -> consumer` boundary is a host
00029| // `Context::wait()` because there is nothing else on this device to order them
00030| // with (A24, Probe B: `zeDeviceGetCommandQueueGroupProperties` reports exactly
00031| // one COMPUTE group with `numQueues = 1`). The waits are counted and reported
00032| // (`step_chunk_waits()`) rather than hidden, because at a measured 22.35 us
00033| // each they are a real term in the chunk's cost.
00034| namespace runtime::prefill {
00035| namespace {
00036| 
00037| using loader::DeviceWeight;
00038| using loader::LoadedModel;
00039| using model::LinearId;
00040| using model::Qwen35;
00041| 
00042| void require(bool ok, const std::string& what) {
00043|   if (!ok) throw std::runtime_error("runtime::prefill::step_chunk: " + what);
00044| }
00045| 
00046| // **The pre-S2a fallback, opt-in through the environment.**
00047| // `B70_PREFILL_SILU_FUSED=0` makes the L0 backend run the old pair -- gate||up
00048| // into the fp32 [C][34816] `partials`, then `pf_silu_mul` -- instead of the
00049| // fused epilogue. It exists so that "before and after" is ONE binary and one
00050| // session rather than two builds, which is the role `B70_PREFILL_GDN_SCAN`
00051| // played for the scan experiment, and so the ABBA that prices this stage can be
00052| // taken without rebuilding between arms.
00053| //
00054| // The fused path is the DEFAULT and is what every gate runs. The two are
00055| // bitwise identical -- `pf_gemm_test`'s silu case compares them directly, on
00056| // device, at M = 2048 and M = 772 -- so this selector chooses a cost, never a
00057| // value. `step_chunk_launches` reads it too, so the launch arithmetic always
00058| // describes the walk that will actually run; `prefill_smoke_test`'s pinned
00059| // constants are the default path's and will fail loudly under `=0`, which is
00060| // the correct behaviour for a knob that changes the list.
00061| bool silu_fused() {
00062|   static const bool on = [] {
00063|     const char* v = std::getenv("B70_PREFILL_SILU_FUSED");
00064|     return v == nullptr || std::strcmp(v, "0") != 0;
00065|   }();
00066|   return on;
00067| }

00069| uint8_t* at(const l0::Mem& m, size_t off) {
00070|   return static_cast<uint8_t*>(m.ptr()) + off;
00071| }
00072| const void* at_const(const l0::Mem& m, size_t off) {
00073|   return static_cast<const uint8_t*>(m.ptr()) + off;
00074| }

00076| // One int4 linear on the prefill path -- THE seam of spec 2.1 §3.2. The sycl-tla side is
00077| // spec 2's two-pass path unchanged (backend_sycl.cc); the L0 side is S2's slab walk.
00078| void pf_linear(Context& cx, KernelCache& kc, PrefillScratch& s, const DeviceWeight& w,
00079|                const uint16_t* x, uint32_t M, PrefillBackend backend) {

00081|     linear_sycl(cx, kc, s, w, x, M);
00082|     return;
00083|   }
00084|   linear_l0(cx, kc, s, w, x, M);
00085| }
